# Privacy deny-list — patterns that must never appear in this repository.
#
# See docs/17-privacy.md. This repository is public: it documents a product, never its owner.
# CI fails on a match; the same scan runs as a pre-commit hook.
#
# This file is itself public, so it contains PATTERNS, not secrets — identifier *shapes*
# rather than real identifiers.
#
# Format: one extended-regex per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# Paths in .privacyignore are excluded from the scan.

# --- External workspace identifiers ------------------------------------------
# Notion-style page/database IDs: 32 hex characters, dashed or bare.
[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}
\b[0-9a-f]{32}\b

# Workspace and share URLs for the external tools.
(notion\.so|notion\.site|app\.notion\.com)/
todoist\.com/(app|showTask|project)
collection://
formulaCode://
collectionProperty://

# Todoist-style numeric object IDs in a task/project context. This is the v9
# shape; `id` and `parent_id` were always missing from it, and the task tool's
# `v1` API (see packages/connectors) replaced the numeric ids with opaque
# 16-character alphanumeric ones — so this pattern alone stopped covering the
# very identifiers it exists for. Both are kept: numeric ids still appear on
# labels, and in anything recorded before the migration.
(task_id|project_id|section_id)["'= :]+[0-9]{8,}

# The v1 shape, in the positions an identifier is written. The leading `\b` is
# load-bearing: without it this matches `operationId: 'createInitiative'`
# (`Id` plus an exactly-16-character camelCase value).
\b(id|task_id|project_id|section_id|parent_id)["'= :]+[0-9A-Za-z]{16}\b

# The same shape under a camelCase key, which the pattern above does not cover:
# `projectId` has no word boundary before its `Id`, so `\bid` never reaches it.
# This is the shape TypeScript and JSON use, which is where a third-party
# response would be pasted.
#
# It requires the value to be **quoted**, and that is the whole of the design.
# The separator alone cannot tell a value from an expression: `projectId:
# parentExternalId` is a sixteen-character camelCase token in an id position,
# and so is a destructuring rename — both are code, not data, and matching
# either is a false positive that would make the pattern useless. A quoted
# string literal is the tell, and it is the only one available here: this
# scanner is `grep -E`, which has no lookahead to express "and not an
# identifier".
#
# What it therefore does **not** cover, stated rather than discovered: an
# unquoted camelCase value (`projectId: 6X7fH2kQ9pLmN3rT` in YAML or JSON5), and
# a quoted value that happens to be an all-letters sixteen-character word. The
# snake_case pattern above covers the unquoted case wherever the key is
# snake_case, which is what those formats normally use.
\b(id|taskId|projectId|sectionId|parentId)["']?[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*["'][0-9A-Za-z]{16}\b

# --- Personal identifiers ----------------------------------------------------
# Generic shapes only. Specific names and addresses belong in
# .github/privacy-denylist.local.txt, which is gitignored and read by the same
# scan — writing them here would publish the very strings we are protecting.
[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@(gmail|outlook|hotmail|yahoo|proton)\.[a-z]{2,}
\+[0-9]{2}\s?[0-9]{9,}

# --- Infrastructure details --------------------------------------------------
# Internal hostnames, private addresses and secret-store paths belong to the
# deployment repository, never here. Variable NAMES are fine; values are not.
\b(10|192\.168)\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\b
# Internal hostnames only in host position — a bare "\.local\b" also matches
# filename globs like *.local.* and denylist.local.txt, which are not hostnames.
(https?://|@|[[:space:]])[a-z0-9-]+\.(local|lan|internal)([:/[:space:]]|$)
(vault|secret)/(data|kv)/
kubeconfig

# --- Instance data ------------------------------------------------------------
# Names of databases and boards in the live workspace. prisme addresses external
# stores by role key (objectives_db, takeaways_db, …) precisely so these never
# need to appear — see docs/17-privacy.md.
#
# Note: "département de vie" is deliberately NOT listed. It is generic French
# domain vocabulary and appears once, by design, in the FR↔EN glossary in
# docs/10-model.md. A concrete *list* of areas or their weights is instance data;
# the term for the concept is not.
Objectifs Tracking
Takeaways - Life Actions
Information Media
Goals Review - (Weekly|Monthly|Quarterly|Yearly)
T[âa]ches Board
Projets Board
Automation Notion-Todoist
